a field guide to the

Night Sounds of the Russet Nexus

The eight sounds most often reported by people trying to sleep in the lower and eastern chambers, with sonograms, mnemonics and range maps.

Volume one · recorded on the night of 17–18 November

How to use this guide

Tap a sonogram to hear it. A sonogram shows pitch going up and time going across, so a whistle is a line, a click is a stripe, and a hiss is a cloud. The darker the mark, the louder the sound.

All recordings were made from one microphone hung at the tube junction, between 23:10 and 05:40, and none of them has been cleaned up. The faint rumble under everything is the bunker.

On a phone, the silent switch silences the bunker too.

The mnemonics are how the sounds are written down by people who hear them a lot. Say them out loud. It helps.

1

Chandelier potato

Solanum pendulum
Resident. Common.
Voice
A low, steady hum near 61 Hz, with a bright buzz of overtones stacked above it. Two of them hang close together over the east stair, slightly out of tune with each other, so the hum swells and fades about once every 1.4 seconds. Never stops.
Mnemonic
mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm (continues)
Similar sounds
The refrigerator, which stops.
Notes
Some visitors can’t handle it. They aren’t asked back, and they don’t ask.
2

Pneumatic capsule P-7, in transit

Capsula festinans
Mealtimes. Locally abundant.
Voice
A hiss that climbs in pitch and loudness for three seconds as it comes closer, with a tick or two at the tube joints, then nothing at all while it takes the bend. Arrival is one soft, low thunk, followed by a short sigh from the seal.
Mnemonic
hssssSSSSSS . . . dup. pff.
Similar sounds
None, once you’ve heard it.
Notes
Heard mostly at mealtimes. After 2 a.m. it’s usually the sloth’s briefcase being sent somewhere. There is a card in the seat pocket for if it stops.
3

Fermentation crock

Olla bullans
Resident. Abundant in warm weather.
Voice
Single low bloops at no fixed interval, each one bending slightly upward at the end, sometimes two close together. It is a bubble closing over itself at the surface of a crock.
Mnemonic
blp. . . . . . blp-blop. . . . . . . . blp.
Similar sounds
A stomach in a library.
Notes
There are 211 crocks in the caverns. Nobody has found which one this is.
4

Nightlight, changing mode

Solanum andigenum, 400 yrs., in mineral oil
Resident. Bedroom only.
Voice
One dry tick, then a faint glassy ring that dies away over about two seconds while the oil settles. Given once for each change of mode.
Mnemonic
tk. (iiiiiiing)
Similar sounds
A fingernail on a wine glass, but kinder.
Notes
There are 47 modes. Nobody has heard all of them in one night. This recording is 31 going to 32.
5

Bioluminescent beetle, wing-case click

Lampyris telegraphica
Resident. Ceilings generally.
Voice
Very short, dry clicks, either alone or run together into a quick buzz, arranged long and short. The beetles spell their warnings out in light. This is the sound their wing cases make while they do it.
Mnemonic
tzz tzz . tk tk . tk tzz tk tk . tzz tk tzz
Similar sounds
Rain on a tin roof, if the rain had something to say.
Notes
Transcribed as morse: — —  /  · ·  /  · — · ·  /  — · —. Decoded, this one says MILK. The milk was fine. They’re usually right, so we keep checking.
6

Sentient mash dispenser, reading a mood

Machina purea
Resident. Kitchen of Infinite Forms.
Voice
Three low, nasal hums, each lower than the one before, the first two turned up at the end like questions. A pause. Then one wet, final splat.
Mnemonic
hm? hm? hmmm . . . . splat.
Similar sounds
A doctor reading your chart.
Notes
The third hum depends on who’s listening. If it goes up, you’re getting the purple. In this recording it goes down, which is yukon gold with extra butter.
7

The sloth, nodding

on the second stair
Resident. Rare (about once a fortnight).
Voice
One long creak from the second stair as he leans forward, built out of hundreds of tiny slips, quickening in the middle and slowing again as the nod arrives. The full call lasts about three hours. This recording has been sped up 1,080 times.
Mnemonic
crrrrrreeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeaak
Similar sounds
The second stair with nobody on it, which is quicker.
Notes
At natural speed it is below the threshold of hearing, and of most people’s patience. If you were there for it, it was for you.
8

Cauliflower

Brassica oleracea var. botrytis
Introduced. Not native.
Voice
None recorded.
Mnemonic
—
Similar sounds
Silence. Easily confused with it.
Notes
Silent. This is what it wants you to think. The mark at 2.8 seconds is probably the recorder.

Colophon

No microphone was involved. Every sound in this guide was synthesized from scratch in numpy, sample by sample, and every sonogram was computed from the exact sound beside it, with one calibration for all eight, so a blank one really is blank.

Volume two (upper chambers, the Hydroponic Chapel, the King Edward pod turning over) is in preparation, pending a longer cable.

— spudnik, from the Russet Nexus
